title: The Amount Collected When a Resort Lodging Folio Is Settled
content:
The amount collected from the household when a Resort Lodging folio is settled is what is still to be collected on it: every room rate, resort, incidental and fee charge standing on the folio less every payment already collected against it, taken from the payment route the household names. A deposit standing against the reservation is not one of those charges: it is money already held, and it is set against what is left rather than counted as something owed. The amount is carried at full precision and the payment is rounded to the nearest cent once, at the end. An amount that falls exactly halfway between two cents is rounded to the cent whose last digit is even, which is the convention the collective's finance office settles every folio on.

The amount collected at departure is fixed only after the folio carries the room rate retained for the nights of the stay the party gave up. It is worked out only once the folio carries the departure services charge the stay owes for servicing the unit and for its nightly extras. Before it is worked out, the folio must carry the resort charge owed for the nights of the stay.

## The order in which what is still to be collected is reduced

What is still to be collected is reduced in a fixed order: first the charges held back for the duty manager, then what the household's dining plan meets, then the deposit standing against the reservation, and last the resort credit the household holds, and what is left after all four is the amount collected. Each of the four acts on what the one before it left, and none of them may take the amount collected below nothing.

### A worked settlement (hypothetical figures)

Take a folio carrying 4200.00 USD of room rate, resort, incidental and fee charges together, against which 1200.00 USD of payments has already been collected. What is still to be collected is 4200.00 USD less 1200.00 USD, which is 3000.00 USD.

That 3000.00 USD is then reduced in the order given, each of the four acting on what the one before it left and none of them taking the figure below nothing, and what is left after all four is rounded to the nearest cent once, at the end, as the amount collected.
